solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One miserable squat, head off for good

indicators.note: taking the head off a word and putting something in its place for it means swapping the first letter

parts.note: to squat is to crouch down
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy squatting in a building is evicted for good behaviour, or for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The C at the head of CROUCH comes off and G takes its place, giving GROUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouch is a grumbling, bad-tempered person, one who is perpetually miserable.

clue.text: See someone regularly stayed out after work

indicators.note: after says the following piece is placed behind the earlier one in the answer

parts.note: a machine that works is said to go

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of order, as in a joint that is put out

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps staying out late after work must be seeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To go steady is the idiom for being in a regular romantic relationship with one person.

clue.text: I draw out the borders of Bucks

indicators.note: drawing out a word's borders means pulling away its first and last letters

parts.note: bones is American slang for dollars, or bucks

explanation.surface: An artist sketches the boundaries of Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks looks like the English county (Buckinghamshire); here it is dollars, and BONES loses its outer letters to leave ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral I stands for the number one.

clue.text: Star once snapped hugging posh mistress

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round another piece, which sits inside
something snapped is broken, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech

explanation.surface: A former celebrity is photographed by paparazzi with his arms around his upmarket mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a kept woman of wealthy or noble lovers, a mistress in the old sense.

clue.text: Impound E after busting dealer's premises

indicators.note: busting breaks the given letters apart so they can be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Police seize ecstasy after raiding a drug dealer's property.
explanation.walkthrough: E looks like ecstasy in the drug-raid picture, but it is just one more letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An opium den is a place where opium is sold and smoked, so a drug dealer's premises.

clue.text: Cops, they just get under King Edward's skin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old slang for police officers, after Sir Robert Peel

definitions.text: they just get under King Edward's skin
definitions.meaning: second meaning: kitchen tools that remove a thin layer from a potato

explanation.walkthrough: King Edward sounds royal, but it is a popular British potato variety; the tools strip only its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelers were the first Metropolitan Police officers, and a peeler is also a utensil for paring vegetables.

clue.text: A French joint that's out of fashion

parts.note: un is French for a
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A French cannabis cigarette is hopelessly passé.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhip is slang for uncool or square, lacking current style.

clue.text: Worry one's still into The Dandy

indicators.note: into says the earlier pieces go inside the later one

parts.note: a dude is a dandy, a man fussy about his clothes
one is I, and one's is read as one is: I plus S
still and quiet both mean calm and silent

explanation.surface: Fretting that one remains a fan of the old British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a long-running British comic, which hides the plain meaning of a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Disquietude is a formal noun for anxiety or unease, a state of worry.

clue.text: Bolshie academic turned dumb yes-man?

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a Bolshie, or Bolshevik, is a red, a communist
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A rebellious lecturer has become a silent sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumb is part of the picture: a nodder agrees without words.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodder is someone who nods along to everything, a compliant yes-man.

clue.text: Broadcast caught by young Afghan couple

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it

parts.note: a young Afghan hound is a puppy, or pup
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A transmission is intercepted by a youthful Afghan couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Afghan looks like a person from Afghanistan; it is the breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair up is to join together in twos, which is to couple as a verb.

clue.text: Bet you'll get place set up as a home

indicators.note: the rearranged letters serve as a home, so another piece lives inside them
up as in stirred up: the letters before it are disturbed into new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U sounds like you, the text-speak spelling

explanation.surface: A wager that you will be given somewhere set up as a house to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to gamble on an uncertain outcome, so to bet.

clue.text: Some of those days for wearing tights?

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Some of those days are the ones for putting on tights.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as playful: hose is an old word for tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosed can mean clad in hose, that is, wearing stockings or tights.

clue.text: I once quoted something thrilling

parts.note: if I once did something, I am an ex-doer of it: ex means former
one who quoted is a citer

explanation.surface: I once quoted a thrilling line.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a self-description: I once quoted, so I am an ex-citer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciter is anything that excites or stimulates, a thrilling thing.

clue.text: Assembly of folk brought together by crime, say

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a crime
say, as in for example: crime is one example of a calling or career

explanation.surface: A gathering of people united by lawbreaking, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads crime as a career choice: a con vocation, one example of a calling.
explanation.definitionFit: A convocation is a formal gathering summoned together, such as a church or university assembly.

clue.text: Support eastern lover sanctioned by the law

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a spouse is a partner in a legally recognised marriage

explanation.surface: Back an oriental romance that has legal approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt and support it.

clue.text: Run into Nordic goths? They're sweet and flaky

parts.note: Danish people are Nordic

indicators.note: into says the first piece goes inside a later one

parts.note: goths cultivate a pale look, so they are pasties, pasty-faced people
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into Scandinavian goths, who turn out to be charming but unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet and flaky reads as a character sketch of the goths; it describes pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish pastries are sugary laminated pastries whose dough bakes into flakes.

clue.text: Balance poor in paper's last piece, dear me!

indicators.note: poor suggests a bad state, so the letters it governs are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: last piece means only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of paper
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay at the final article in a newspaper with a weak bank balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The balance is what is left over, the remainder, as of a sum or debt.

clue.text: A great many in Slough look extremely annoyed

parts.note: to slough is to cast off, as a snake sheds its skin
lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the outermost letters at each end

parts.note: the first and last letters of annoyed

explanation.surface: Many people in Slough look very irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town west of London; here it is the verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shedload is informal British slang for a large quantity.

clue.text: Sad result of lark blowing up in one's face?

definitions.text: result of lark blowing up in one's face?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: if a bird exploded in your face you would have feathers in your mouth

explanation.walkthrough: A lark is a prank that can backfire, but here it is the songbird, and down is its soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a downcast, glum expression, so it means unhappy.

clue.text: Sound nervous at first and all of a quiver?

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of nervous
a quiver is a case for arrows, so all its contents are arrows

explanation.surface: A noise that is unsettling at first and makes everything tremble.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like noise; it is the geographical sound, a sea channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of water, and narrows is a word for such a strait.

clue.text: Having an aversion to metal, hand silver over

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hand

indicators.note: over as in covering: one piece is laid round another

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A dislike of metal, so passing over the silverware instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hating something means detesting it, which is having a strong aversion to it.

clue.text: Sign that woman's morning is behind time

indicators.note: is behind says the earlier pieces follow the later one in the answer

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
her is the possessive for that woman
am is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A sign that a woman's morning is running late.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Treasure Her Majesty — she's a keeper

parts.note: a hoard is a store of treasure
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Cherish the Queen: she is worth holding on to.
explanation.walkthrough: Treasure reads as a verb, cherish, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder is someone who keeps and stores things rather than throwing them away.

clue.text: Live to be successful, but at love's expense

indicators.note: at something's expense means it is lost or sacrificed, so it is taken out

parts.note: to do well is to be successful
love is nil, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Living to achieve success, but sacrificing romance along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there.

clue.text: Posterior trouble, see nurse about it

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round another

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sore backside: go and see the nurse about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Posterior is a noun in the surface, a backside, which the answer also names.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail end is the rear part of anything, the posterior.

clue.text: Lug around boxes heartless idiots bring up

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, the way a box holds its contents
around means turned about, read from the other end

parts.note: lug is British slang for ear

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is cut away, keeping only the ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of idiots

explanation.surface: Fools lifting and hauling boxes around.
explanation.walkthrough: Lug and bring up look like heavy lifting; lug is slang for ear, and boxes encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a topic or a child is to bring it up.

clue.text: Euro put-down wrong, BoJo finally admitted

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are in an incorrect order and must be fixed

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for euro
taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of BoJo, nickname of Boris Johnson

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson finally confessed that his insult to the European currency was mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Euro is only its abbreviation, not four letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess or admit it.

clue.text: Where some of the flock rest, quiet sheep mostly

definitions.text: Where some of the flock rest

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: p, piano, means quiet in music
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Where some of the herd lie down, a calm and mostly ovine scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The flock is a church congregation, not sheep, despite the sheep in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pew is a church bench where members of the congregation sit.

clue.text: Irrational to cut down on babysitting?

parts.note: to mind children is to babysit
to cut down on something is to do it less

explanation.surface: Is it unreasonable to reduce the hours spent looking after children?
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting down on babysitting means you would mind (children) less.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless actions lack thought or reason, so they are irrational.

clue.text: Welsh-supplied strain used to make beer

indicators.note: supplied with something means it is put in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a breed is a strain of animal
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: A yeast strain from Wales is used in beer-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewed describes a drink made by brewing, the process that makes beer.
